Traditional ML requires rebuilding models for each task, while foundation models allow rapid adaptation to new tasks through prompting or lightweight fine-tuning. Foundation models require massive resources for pre-training but amortize this cost across many applications, while traditional models have lower per-model costs but higher cumulative costs. This approach continues to evolve as researchers and practitioners develop new techniques and methodologies.
